answer.rationale: P99 latency spiked 5x in 90 minutes immediately after a release 2 hours ago during peak settlement traffic (heavy writes). memory_b1 demonstrates rollback successfully cleared a checkout error spike with the prior stable build and no customer impact. memory_b2 warns against regional failover while writes are hot—this is exactly our situation (settlement peak, heavy writes), so failover is contraindicated. Adding capacity or routing reads won't address a latency regression in the write path caused by the release itself. Circuit breakers help contain dependency failures, not write-path latency from bad code. Rollback is the lowest-risk intervention: it removes the likely culprit, preserves all writes (critical during settlement peak), and memory_b1 shows this has worked before. If rollback succeeds, we return to stable baseline. If it doesn't, we still have capacity and failover options for the next window.
